name: Vega 2
payload: Halley flyby bus + Venus descent module (lander and balloon), ~4,900 kg
significance: Vega 2 repeated its twin's double mission a few days behind it. Its Venus lander reached the surface and analysed a soil sample, and its balloon added a second track through the clouds, so the two together gave the first measurements of wind across a large stretch of the Venusian atmosphere. At Halley it passed even closer than Vega 1, refining the comet's position for Giotto and confirming that the nucleus was a single dark, irregular body rather than the double object the first blurry images had suggested.
statusNote: Twin of Vega 1, launched 1984-12-21. Descent module entered Venus's atmosphere on 1985-06-15 (lander ~57 min of surface data at Rusalka Planitia; balloon floated ~46 h). The bus flew past Venus at ~24,500 km and passed Halley's nucleus at 8,030 km on 1986-03-09 07:20 UT. Contact ended 1987-03-24. Modeled as Lambert legs between the real launch, Venus flyby and Halley encounter dates; no JPL Horizons ephemeris exists. Sources: NASA NSSDCA (COSPAR 1984-128A; nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/planets/cometpage.html), the mission's Wikipedia article and its cited references (Siddiqi 2018, Beyond Earth, NASA SP-2018-4041), and agency pages.
